title: Small Tools
subtitle: Small tools for engineering, research, resumes, and agents.
description: As AI becomes part of everyday work and learning, a personal set of skills and tools can preserve habits, workflows, and judgment while reducing repeated setup and rework.
viewAllDescription: Browse tools for context, research, and agents.

typelift.title: TypeLift
typelift.summary: A lightweight macOS translator that stays inside your typing flow. Summon a floating input, choose between a fast, cost-conscious translation API and a more capable language-model API, then send the result straight back to the original cursor.
points: Stay in your flow with a global shortcut, a floating input, automatic input-source switching, and translations returned directly to the original cursor

Balance speed, cost, and capability with standard translation for fast, economical results and language-model translation for deeper context and more expressive wording, then press Tab to switch whenever both are available
Write for different situations with built-in Natural, Concise, Formal, and Social styles, or add, reorder, rename, and tailor styles of your own
Make TypeLift work your way by setting source, target, and interface languages, choosing how its menu bar and Dock icons behave, and prioritizing floating-window placement strategies

prompt-sketch.title: PromptSketch
prompt-sketch.summary: A lightweight sketchpad for showing AI what you mean. Paste a screenshot or start with a blank canvas, mark it up in seconds, then copy or save the result.
points: No sign-up or uploads—open the page and start drawing.
Use freehand strokes, whole-stroke erasing, and simple shapes to annotate screenshots or sketch from scratch.
Undo, redo, shortcuts, zoom, and pan keep the workflow quick with a mouse, trackpad, or stylus.
Copy the finished canvas or save it as an image for prompts, messages, and documents.

project-context-meta-skill.title: Project Context Meta-Skill
project-context-meta-skill.summary: A personal meta-skill for building AI-native engineering environments. Three decoupled subsystems provide structured project context and help the AI question, reason, and weigh trade-offs independently.
points: Uses structured project memory to keep long conversations from losing key facts or repeating past mistakes.
Preserves raw requirements and specs so the AI can anchor on the user's root goals and original intent.
Reminds the AI that requirements may be unclear, so it should guide, challenge, reason from goals and code, offer trade-offs, and avoid over-engineering.
Indirectly preserves task-specific prompts so they can be traced, migrated, and learned from.
Captures the problems and reflections I accumulated while using AI tools.

research-skills.title: Engineering Research Skills
research-skills.summary: A research workflow for engineering, product, market, and scientific judgment when questions are broad, information is noisy, and the result must still support a decision.
points: Turns ad hoc searching into a reusable process across Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and similar AI tools.
Uses AnySearch as the real-time retrieval entry for technical selection, product analysis, competitor research, papers, and open-source evaluation.
Requires outputs to include not only collected facts, but also evidence, boundaries, risks, and actionable recommendations.
Turns uncertain information into engineering material that can be discussed, decided on, and carried forward.

latex-resume.title: LaTeX Resume Builder
latex-resume.summary: A private in-progress LaTeX resume project for multilingual, role-targeted resumes. It keeps language variants, role emphasis, and length constraints from drifting out of sync.
points: Separates experience, project descriptions, skill phrasing, and layout for Chinese, English, and other variants.
Supports fast role adaptation by changing emphasis without manually rebuilding each file.
Uses LaTeX for stable formatting and version control, treating the resume as a long-lived content asset.
May eventually become a skill, template system, or another automation tool for a reusable job-search material workflow.

anysearch-skill.title: AnySearch Skill
anysearch-skill.summary: A real-time search engine skill for AI agents, supporting web search, vertical search, batch search, and full-page extraction.
points: Provides search capability to AI agents through an API, focusing on quality, speed, and customizability.
Supports Python, Node.js, PowerShell, and Shell to reduce integration friction across agent environments.
Fixed the agent's discovery and invocation of Python scripts; the contribution has been merged upstream.

crater-prompt.title: Crater Agent Prompts
crater-prompt.summary: Agent working prompts accumulated for Crater before formal Skills became common. They help AI enter a complex project's context, rules, and constraints without relearning everything each time.
points: Turns Crater development experience, recurring requirements, and collaboration habits into working instructions that can be given directly to AI.
Helps agents enter the existing engineering context faster, reducing invalid work and repeated communication.
Externalizes implicit experience into a reusable collaboration entry point.

tododag.title: ToDoDAG
tododag.summary: An early task-manager concept for work that does not fit a flat to-do list. It maps dependencies as a DAG so I can see what is actionable now and what is still blocked.
points: Turns a long backlog into a graph of prerequisites, blockers, and newly unlocked work.
Keeps sudden ideas, assigned tasks, and long-term plans together without losing their dependencies.
Planned as a native, local-first Apple app with private iCloud sync across devices.
Still at the planning and prototype stage, with AI-assisted task execution being explored.
